title: Upgrade Safeguard: Micro-eval Harness and Cross-Version Compatibility Prober
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a lightweight, fast micro-eval harness that runs deterministic cross-version compatibility probes and quick perf sanity checks as a preflight step prior to any LTS or stable channel release. The harness must be fast enough to run inside pre-release pipelines and provide clear 'go/no-go' signals for rollout gates (canary -> staged -> full).
background: Current preflight suites are large and take hours; they are effective but slow and expensive to run for every patch. Our LTS channel changes require an early-warning signal for regressions in model outputs, tokenization, KV cache behavior, and latency tail events. A micro-eval harness will reduce time-to-feedback and give the release team a compact, actionable summary for rollouts.
goals: 1) Provide deterministic compatibility checks across runtime versions and model variants. 2) Surface tokenization drift and output-format regressions. 3) Detect KV-cache deserialization/compatibility issues via fingerprint tests. 4) Catch 95th/99th percentile latency regressions with lightweight synthetic trace replay. 5) Produce a single-pass pass/fail gate with detailed artifacts for debugging.
non_goals: This ticket does not replace full-scale perf/eval suites or customer canary programs. It should not attempt exhaustive model quality evaluation against production prompt distributions.
implementation_notes:
- Implement harness as a containerized job that can be executed in CI and on the release validation runners.
- Tests are organized into three buckets: correctness probes (deterministic prompts + tokenization hashes), KV-compat probes (small sequence of requests that stress cache load/save boundaries), and latency probes (short synthetic trace replay with controlled concurrency).
- Each probe emits a compact JSON artifact: input_id, baseline_hash, observed_hash, latency_ms_p50_p95_p99, failure_reason.
- Add a small orchestration layer to run probes against 'candidate' and 'baseline' binaries and diff results.
- Include a reproducible seed for prompts and a fixed model version list for stability.
- Keep runtime under 12 minutes for default runs; allow extended mode for deeper checks.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for probe encoders and hashers. 2) Integration in a disposable k8s namespace with 3 small single-GPU nodes. 3) Run harness against current prod runtime (baseline) and feature branch (candidate) and confirm expected pass. 4) Inject synthetic faults (KV inversion, tokenization offset) to validate failure detection. 5) Validate artifact upload to the release dashboard and linking to a debug playbook.
acceptance_criteria:
- Harness produces a 'Gate Verdict' artifact (PASS/FAIL) with a summary table in < 12 minutes for default config.
- Detected regressions include clear diff output and a reproducible failing input.
- Latency regressions are flagged if p95 increases > 15% or p99 increases > 10% vs baseline.
- KV cache incompatibility is flagged when fingerprint mismatch > 0 for any saved/restored state.
- On first run against runtime-1.18 candidate, no high-severity issues should appear; any medium/high failures require blocking the rollout until triaged.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (internal CI): enable harness as a required preflight for all release candidate merges to release branches. Phase 2 (release validation): run harness in the preflight pipeline that gates canary deployments. Phase 3 (post-rollout): run nightly regression micro-evals against LTS snapshots to detect drift.
Rollback policy: if harness returns FAIL during canary gate, halt the staged rollout and create a high-priority incident with the harness artifacts attached.
metrics:
- Mean time to verdict (minutes).
- False positive rate (alerts that are later triaged as non-issues).
- Detected regressions per month.
- Median and 95th/99th latency deltas reported by harness.
- Percentage of releases gated by harness results.
dashboard_and_alerting: Create a release-validation dashboard tile that shows latest harness verdict, latency deltas, and top failing input IDs. Wire a Slack channel #release-harness with automated posts for FAIL verdicts. Attach direct links from the tile to the CI artifact and GitHub PR.
safety_considerations: Harness will not hit production datasets. Use synthetic prompt corpus and only run against non-customer data. Ensure KMS keys are not used by test jobs and artifacts are scrubbed of any sensitive tokens.
dependencies_notes: Depends on ENG-10824 for improved smoke perf eval harness shims and ENG-31207 for compatibility prober libraries; coordinate API shapes and artifact formats with those tasks.
